summary: Completed frontend-only regression and UX validation across all 18 routes (desktop/mobile), key workspace/landing interactions, and route-level overflow checks. Core flows are working, with one confirmed mobile overflow regression on dashboard submetrics.

ui_bugs.issue: Document horizontal overflow persists on /dashboard at 390x844 (scrollWidth 477 > clientWidth 390). Overflow originates from .submetric-item/.submetric-text/.submetric-val region.

integration_issues.issue: Multiple frontend API requests return 502 (health, alerts, marine, chat, ml dashboard). UI fallback/preview mode behaves as designed.

issues: Horizontal scrolling caused by submetric strip layout conflict between legacy styles.css and ocean-system.css mobile overrides.

action_items: Fix dashboard mobile overflow by reconciling segmented submetric layout rules (legacy grid vs mobile flex intent).
If keeping smooth scrolling globally, add Next.js recommended html data-scroll-behavior attribute to remove warning noise.
Confirm /app/orca-build.log includes a complete successful build output (current file appears partial/truncated).
critical_code_review_comments: styles.css (~9843 lines) and ocean-system.css currently overlap on shared selectors; this creates cascade conflicts (confirmed in segmented-status-row mobile behavior).
In ocean-system.css mobile override, segmented-status-row sets flex-direction without explicitly changing display from legacy grid, so intended stacking does not reliably apply.
Large global stylesheet size and duplicate selector ownership increase regression risk during incremental redesign.
seed_data_creation: No backend seed data created. UI-created local notices tested only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 18 routes render at 1920 widths with no document overflow. Landing controls, theme/language persistence, Ctrl+K routing, sidebar collapse/mobile drawer, dashboard widget persistence, fishing route forwarding, and map control surface are working. Dashboard still has real mobile overflow from submetric strip (non-Leaflet cause). Alerts acknowledge button is state-dependent label ('Acknowledge Bulletin' or 'Mark as Unacknowledged'). Backend is unavailable and frontend runs in preview/fallback mode.
rca of the issue: Reproduced at 390x844 on /dashboard: document scrollWidth 477 vs clientWidth 390. Offending elements are within segmented-status-row (.submetric-item -> .submetric-text -> .submetric-val). Root cause is CSS cascade conflict: legacy styles.css defines segmented-status-row as 3-column grid, while ocean-system.css mobile override applies flex-direction/alignments without forcing display:flex; mobile intent does not fully override grid behavior, causing content spill. Mitigation: in mobile breakpoint explicitly set display:flex (or single-column grid) with width-safe child constraints and retest at 390x844.
